v3_delta_check: Partly applied, and the coordinator's identity claim is slightly off. Of the 36 sampled cases already reviewed in v2, 32 are identical apart from the verification block. Four are not byte-identical: binary_search-da1b555b76a6, chunk-c09f2ed58720, longest_run-dfcbc3f4926b and merge_sorted-e86597f49d02. Each changed only difficulty, medium to easy, which is the intended change; I checked it. Rows: v2 had 74 and v3 has 71. Three were dropped and none added. Rejection ledger: 15 entries, which are the 12 earlier compile/fail/regression rejections plus three new ones. (1) rotate_left-v2-0ec61f37bdc1 is excluded manually, with my TypeError reason quoted. (2) median-v2-34d4437b4580 is dropped as a behavioural duplicate, which is correct. (3) sign-v2-fce1582ed832 is also dropped as a behavioural duplicate. That one is correct too: the authored sign bug ends with 'return 1', so at 0 it returns 1, exactly like n>=0. I had accepted fce1582 in v2 without seeing that authored row; this drop corrects my oversight. The dedup (build.py dedupe_by_behaviour) keys on outcome_sha256 of [test_id, returned, value] over the suite's tests. Category counts are consistent with the drops: operator 25 to 23, comparison 18 to 17. All 18 mutants are 'easy', and every mutant's category matches the edited-construct rule. NOT applied: my v2 notes on authored rows. caesar_shift is still medium/operator, chunk and median are still medium, transpose is still medium while flatten is easy, and is_even is still 'operator'. All 9 medium rows are authored. The general crash-only filter was not added; only the one manual exclusion was applied. The manifest's limitations field still correctly says the manual audit has not been performed, and the v3 worksheet's manual_review_status is still PENDING.
cross_cutting_findings: No wrong expected values, ambiguous behavior texts or equivalent bugs were found in the 14 new cases. Every recorded baseline matches a hand trace and the copy of the baseline in the row's verification block.

Difficulty and category for authored rows are still assigned by hand and inconsistent. The 'algorithm' category comes with 'easy' for to_binary and unique_sorted but 'medium' for rotate_left, while the fixed rule maps an algorithmic change to hard. The fizzbuzz branch-reorder bug is 'easy' although its branches interact. caesar_shift, chunk, median and transpose remain medium for one local edit. Recommend one rule for authored rows, applied the way the mutant rule now is, with the rationale recorded in the row.

A crash-only rule is needed, not one manual exclusion. longest_run-6ba5a35d6b61 raises IndexError on every input of length 2 or more, and its regression passes only skip the loop. binary_search-20482e2cb554 fails only by IndexError. Suggested rule: require at least one failing test that returns a wrong value, or at least one regression pass that executes the edited line. Then decide whether always-crashing index off-by-ones stay in.

Several suites have trivial regression baselines: equal pairs for maximum and minimum, empty or one-element inputs for reverse_list and word_lengths, and loop-bypassing inputs for longest_run-6ba5. A 'preserve regression tests' reward term is then nearly free for these rows. Recommend that each suite include at least one non-trivial input the bug does not affect.

Behavioural dedup works only on test-observable behaviour. Its key is [test_id, returned, value] over the suite's own inputs, and exceptions collapse to returned=false. Two bugs that differ off-suite, or raise different exception types on the same tests, would be merged. The three drops observed here are truly equivalent programs, so no wrong drop was seen.

Scope and method: the 14 cases were read by hand, along with manifest.json, the v2-to-v3 row diff and build.py. No fixture code was executed and no file was modified. The v3 worksheet sha256 is e5ad3d37daf85fc689ea66b665bce740c864fb3b4d738dc94f9fadcf0754a615. The 32 unchanged cases carry over their v2 verdicts.
